facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of a rapidly enlarging left breast mass
no history of pain, trauma, fever, anorexia, or weight loss
the left breast had a 20 cm × 20 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump
the right breast was normal
the mass was not fixed to skin or underlying muscle
the overlying skin was tense and shiny with prominent superficial veins
no nipple discharge and no axillary lymphadenopathy
Routine hematological and biochemical tests, including ESR, were within normal limits
A chest radiograph was normal
Ultrasonography of the left breast revealed a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern suggestive of fibroadenoma
Fine-needle aspiration cytology of the lump showed pathology suggesting fibroadenoma
fibroadenoma

concepts.why: The patient has a 1-year history of a rapidly enlarging left breast mass with a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern suggestive of fibroadenoma on ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology showing pathology suggesting fibroadenoma.
The patient has a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump in the left breast, which could be consistent with a breast lipoma.
The patient has a rapidly enlarging left breast mass with a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern, which could be consistent with a phyllodes tumor.
The patient has a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump in the left breast, which could be consistent with a breast hamartoma.
The patient is a premenarcheal girl with a rapidly enlarging left breast mass, which could be consistent with a juvenile fibroadenoma.
The patient has a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump in the left breast, which could be consistent with a breast cyst.
The patient has a rapidly enlarging left breast mass with a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern, which could be consistent with pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia.
The patient has a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump in the left breast, which could be consistent with a breast adenoma.

rationales.F01: Rapidly enlarging breast mass suggests a tumor, which could be fibroadenoma or phyllodes tumor.
rationales.F03: Well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump is consistent with fibroadenoma.
rationales.F05: The mass not being fixed to skin or underlying muscle reduces the likelihood of a malignant tumor like phyllodes tumor.
rationales.F06: Tense and shiny skin with prominent superficial veins could indicate a rapidly growing tumor, but is not specific.
rationales.F10: Ultrasonography showing a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern is highly suggestive of fibroadenoma.
rationales.F11: Fine-needle aspiration cytology showing pathology suggestive of fibroadenoma strongly supports this diagnosis.
rationales.F12: Direct mention of fibroadenoma as a diagnosis based on pathology results strongly supports this diagnosis.
